newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo's Sykes warns of UK science decline.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo's Sykes warns of UK science decline.

text.p: - Glaxo Wellcome Plc deputy chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes warned on Monday that a serious decline in the science base could jeopardise Britain's ability to attract and keep high level investment.

In a speech to the Confederation of British Industry (CBI)'s annual conference here, Sykes said the strength of Britain's scientific research had been a key factor in attracting inward investment in pharmaceuticals and other high-tech industries.
Glaxo Wellcome, which is the world's biggest prescription drugs group, opened a 700 million stg research facility in Stevenage, England, last year.

Sykes said that on many measures the UK's attractions as an international base had grown in recent years. "There is, however, growing concern in my industry that a valuable competitive advantage is now being eroded," he said.

The poor quality of scientific equipment available in British universities meant many graduates and post-graduates had "simply had no experience of much of the technology now used in our R&D facilities."
If the decline in investment was not reversed, Sykes said, Britain would "inevitably lose out to competitor nations in the contest to attract and retain investment by science-based industries."
"Public investment in science and technology must be a priority if Britain is to compete successfully in the global marketplace of the 21st Century."
